rules: verified=false means every signals field is null: such a child is a proposal only and must not become a rule.
surface=api: documented vendor API endpoint (scripts, integrations). The first-party web UI's own request paths are not documented and must not be assumed equal.
host_sni lists names as the source spells them; a '*.' or '{...}' form is a pattern, not a literal.
path_pattern alternatives are separated by ' | '; '{version}' on graph.microsoft.com is v1.0 or beta.
transport is set for non-HTTP signals (ports, UDP media, SSH); those are invisible to an HTTP rule and UDP is off the Phase 1 observed path.
Hosts and paths are client assertions seen by a decrypting proxy, not authenticated identity.

Rows citing raw.githubusercontent.com cite the vendor's own published spec or SDK repository (Asana, Figma, Pinterest, Vimeo, Miro, Canva, Notion, monday.com, Proton, pCloud, Discord, Dropbox), used where the vendor's documentation site was not reachable; each note names the file and the line content.

sec_child_3.finding: Every Gmail upload method has two path forms, '/upload/gmail/v1/...' (simple) and '/resumable/upload/gmail/v1/...' (resumable), both with multipart: true: users.messages.send, users.messages.insert, users.messages.import, users.drafts.create, users.drafts.send (POST) and users.drafts.update (PUT /upload/gmail/v1/users/{userId}/drafts/{id}). uploadType is a query parameter ('Legacy upload protocol for media (e.g. "media", "multipart")'), not a path segment.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: A rule keyed on '/upload/gmail' alone misses '/resumable/upload/gmail'; drafts.update is PUT. Wave 0 rows cover the five POST methods; drafts.update (PUT) is new here.

sec_child_3.finding: 'APIs debut in the beta version and are accessible in the https://graph.microsoft.com/beta endpoint' and v1.0 'in the https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0 endpoint'. URL form '{HTTP method} https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/{resource}?{query-parameters}' (use-the-api).
sec_child_3.engine_impact: Every graph.microsoft.com child path must accept both /v1.0/ and /beta/ as the first segment.

sec_child_3.finding: 'Path URL resource names, query parameters, and action parameters and values are case insensitive. However, values you assign, entity IDs, and other base64-encoded values are case-sensitive.' traverse-the-graph: 'Assume path URL resource names, query parameters, action and function names ... are not case-sensitive.' OneDrive: path identifiers used with colons and filenames in the URL 'are not case-sensitive', but metadata path identifiers such as '/items/{item-id}/image' 'are case-sensitive'.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: Match Graph resource-name segments case-insensitively (/ME/DRIVE/... is /me/drive/...); keep IDs as literal wildcards. The OneDrive page's case-sensitive metadata segments are a narrower exception for that API surface.

sec_child_3.finding: 'Microsoft Graph implements the $batch OData URL path segment'; 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$batch' (or beta); each inner request has a relative 'url' ('while the absolute URL is https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users, this url is /users'); 'JSON batch requests are currently limited to 20 individual requests.' Also: 'On the beta endpoint, the $ prefix is optional' for query options (query-parameters page).
sec_child_3.engine_impact: A $batch POST carries up to 20 operations (methods and paths) in its JSON body, so a path rule sees only '/$batch': either parse the body (bounded by the request budget) or treat $batch as 'any Graph function'.

sec_child_3.finding: Discovery 'batchPath' is 'batch' for gmail.googleapis.com (and for meet, chat, photoslibrary), and 'batch/drive/v3' and 'batch/drive/v2' on www.googleapis.com for Drive.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: POST /batch (or /batch/drive/v3) wraps several API calls in one multipart/mixed body; the inner method and path are not in the outer request line.

sec_child_3.finding: Drive v2 is still published: rootUrl https://www.googleapis.com/, servicePath 'drive/v2/'; files.insert POST simple '/upload/drive/v2/files', resumable '/resumable/upload/drive/v2/files'; files.update PUT '/upload/drive/v2/files/{fileId}' and '/resumable/upload/drive/v2/files/{fileId}'; files.get GET 'files/{fileId}' with media download, files.export GET 'files/{fileId}/export'. v3 uses POST '/upload/drive/v3/files' and PATCH '/upload/drive/v3/files/{fileId}'.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: Drive upload rules need v2 and v3 paths and both POST/PUT (v2) and POST/PATCH (v3) methods.

sec_child_3.finding: 'All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME'; 'All methods in the Bot API are case-insensitive.' Files: 'https://api.telegram.org/file/bot<token>/<file_path>'.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: sendDocument, SENDDOCUMENT and senddocument are the same method: compare the method segment case-insensitively. The path also carries the bot token, which must never be emitted.

sec_child_3.finding: 'You should specify which version to use by including it in the request path like https://discord.com/api/v{version_number}. Omitting the version number from the route will route requests to the current default version (marked below).' Table: v10 Available, v9 Available, v8 and v7 Deprecated, v6 Deprecated and Default, v5 to v3 Discontinued.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: Discord child paths must accept /api/v10/, /api/v9/ (and deprecated v8, v7, v6) and the unversioned /api/ prefix, which routes to v6. Wave 0 rows that name /api/v10 only are too narrow.

sec_child_3.finding: Dropbox's official SDKs: 'Download style means that the route argument goes in a Dropbox-API-Arg header'; upload style sets Content-Type 'application/octet-stream' and the Dropbox-API-Arg header; RPC style is 'application/json'. Hosts: API_CONTENT_HOST 'content' + '.dropboxapi.com', API_HOST 'api' + '.dropboxapi.com' (session.py). The JS SDK sends method POST with headers['Dropbox-API-Arg'] for download and upload.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: The file path and options of a Dropbox upload or download are in the Dropbox-API-Arg header (JSON), not in the URL; both directions are POST to content.dropboxapi.com.

sec_child_3.finding: UNVERIFIED: whether content endpoints also accept the argument as a URL query parameter 'arg' (and 'authorization') is stated, if anywhere, in the HTTP documentation's 'Formats' section on www.dropbox.com, which is SOURCE BLOCKED (row 48). Not in the SDK files read.
sec_child_3.engine_impact: Until read, a rule must not assume the header is the only place the argument can appear.
